projects.title: FORMA
projects.summary: A 3D-printed modular joint system for student and renter furniture.
projects.body:
Forma — Swedish for 'to shape, form, or build'. Nomadic furniture concept aimed at New Zealand renters and small-space living, inspired by IKEA's accessible, adaptable design ethos. The goal was fast, sustainable, portable furniture built from local materials and 3D-printed joinery.

Research into precedents like Hennessey and Papanek's Nomadic Furniture 3.0 pointed toward flexible, modular, portable systems, while an open-ended 'Sticks and Stones' experiment, giving people wooden sticks and Blu Tack to build furniture freely, showed that creative freedom alone often lacks direction, which shaped the decision to build a guided modular kit instead.

The resulting connector system uses a consistent 16mm diameter across all joints, inspired by PVC fittings and LEGO's single-stud logic, letting 3D-printed connectors and wooden dowels combine into different configurations without screws.

Early prototypes proved unstable with too few connector types, which led to introducing a third component: a laser-cut wooden plate with a grid pattern that distributes load and adds connection points, enabling larger, more stable structures without adding complexity.

The final system, PETG-printed joints, 16mm dowels, and 3mm wooden sheet, packs into a calico carry bag inspired by IKEA's own material language, staying lightweight, portable, and quick to set up.
